goal: Relay CH-04's chat.turn.progress / chat.turn.completed / chat.turn.error Redis pub/sub events to the owning client's live WebSocket connection, under a per-push RBAC re-filter, using the pinned client-facing frame shapes that CH-06 builds against.

acceptanceCriteria.text: For a turn processed while the owner is subscribed, the owner's socket receives the chat.turn.progress frames followed by the chat.turn.completed frame, in publish order, with seq strictly increasing from 1 — proven with a Core stub whose first authorization call resolves more slowly than the second (i.e. ordering survives the async re-filter).

A user in the same org who is not the conversation's owner is refused at subscribe with the generic chat_forbidden error frame, records no subscription, triggers no Redis SUBSCRIBE, and receives nothing when events subsequently flow on that conversation's channel. A connection authenticated under a different org can never match, because matchingChat compares the connection's token-derived orgId against the envelope's org_id.

A chat.turn.completed event whose citation list contains a node id outside the receiving client's current scope is delivered with that citation absent, with the remaining citations intact and metrics byte-identical to the worker's report.

When a connection's scope is reduced after it subscribed, the very next push is filtered under the new scope: with two successive events and an authorization stub that returns a narrower authorizedNodeIds on the second call, the first frame carries the citation and the second does not — and Core was called once per event per connection, not once at subscribe.

{ type:'unsubscribe', channel:'chat', conversationId } and socket close both release the conversation's Redis subscription; after the last subscriber for a channel goes away, chatBus.subscribedChannels() no longer contains it and a real UNSUBSCRIBE was issued exactly once. No connection close leaves a subscription behind.

Contract conformance: for each of the three push types, the frame the client receives has exactly the pinned key set — ['conversationId','detail','kind','seq','tool','ts','turnId','type'], ['answer','citations','conversationId','metrics','ts','turnId','type'], ['code','conversationId','message','ts','turnId','type'] — with each citation carrying exactly ['kind','label','nodeId','resolvedNodeId'] and each metrics object exactly ['baselineTokens','contextNodes','ratio','tokensUsed']. Extra keys present on the incoming worker payload never appear on the wire.

Each of these is dropped with a log and never forwarded to any client: a non-JSON or assertValidEnvelope-failing message; an envelope whose org_id disagrees with the channel's org segment; a payload whose conversationId disagrees with the channel's conversation segment; an envelope whose type is not one of the three pinned types.

The gateway never accepts an org id from client input or trusts one from a message body: the subscribe frame carries no org field, conn.orgId comes only from the verified connection identity, the relay's org comes only from envelope.org_id, and the request body fetchChatPushAuthorization sends contains exactly { conversationId, nodeIds } — no org_id, orgId, userId or token field.

The per-push re-filter is real, not a subscribe-time cache: N events to one subscribed connection produce N authorization calls to Core, each carrying that connection's own bearer token, and the gateway itself performs no scope computation (it only set-intersects against the ids Core returned).

Back-compatibility: every existing test in services/gateway/src/**/*.test.ts passes unchanged, the existing {type:'subscribe', repoId} / {type:'unsubscribe', repoId} frames decode and behave identically, and fanOutGraphUpdated / createGraphUpdatedBus behaviour is untouched.

POST /internal/realtime/chat-authorization returns { conversationId, authorizedNodeIds } for the conversation's owner, returns 404 for both a nonexistent conversation and one owned by another user (indistinguishable), returns 403 for an agent-key subject, and derives org/user solely from the authenticated context — client-supplied org_id / orgId / userId body fields have no effect.

Fail-closed on authorization failure: when the Core authorization call errors (unavailable, non-2xx, or network), that connection receives zero frames for that push — never the unfiltered event and never a partially filtered one — and the subscription is retained for the next event.

chatEventChannel(orgId, conversationId) produces exactly the string CH-04's sayre_workers.chat.events.chat_event_channel produces, and CHAT_EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX is 'sayre:chat.events' — pinned by an explicit test so the two sides cannot drift.

edgeCases.text: Malformed envelope on a chat channel: non-JSON text, a JSON array, or an object missing a required envelope field (assertValidEnvelope throws) — dropped, logged, handler never invoked, connection unaffected.
envelope.org_id differs from the channel's org segment — dropped, logged, never forwarded (even to a connection whose orgId matches one of the two values).
payload.conversationId differs from the channel's conversation segment — dropped, logged, never forwarded.
envelope.type is graph.updated, chat.turn.request, or any other unrecognized value — dropped, logged.
envelope.source is not 'sayre-chat-worker' — dropped, logged.
The received channel string does not match sayre:chat.events:{orgId}:{conversationId} (wrong prefix, too few/many colon segments, blank segment) — dropped, logged.

Structurally invalid payload for its declared type: progress with seq: 0, seq: 1.5, a missing seq, or kind: 'other'; completed with a non-array citations, a citation missing nodeId, a citation with kind: 'function', a non-numeric metrics.ratio, or more than CHAT_MAX_CITATIONS (24) citations; error with a blank code — each dropped, logged.
Subscribe to a conversation id that does not exist — the identical chat_forbidden frame and message a non-owner gets; nothing in the reply distinguishes absent from unowned.

Duplicate subscribe to the same conversation on one connection — both replies are { type:'subscribed', channel:'chat', conversationId }, chatSubscriptions.size stays 1, and acquireChatChannel fired exactly once (one real Redis SUBSCRIBE).
Unsubscribe for a conversation never subscribed on that connection — no throw, no reply frame, releaseChatChannel never called, refcount untouched.

Disconnect mid-turn: the socket closes between two events — releaseChatSubscriptions releases every held channel, the connection is deregistered, and an in-flight relayChatEvent targeting the now-closed socket is a silent no-op (sendSafe's readyState !== OPEN guard), not a crash.

Scope lookup failure at push time — Core returns 500, or fetch rejects — this push delivers nothing to that connection (fail closed), the error is logged without the bearer token, the subscription is retained, and the next event is attempted normally.
Core returns 401 at push time (session expired mid-turn) — onUnauthorized(conn) fires (production wiring closes the socket with UNAUTHENTICATED_CLOSE_CODE) and no event frame is delivered.

Core returns 403 or 404 at push time (ownership revoked or conversation deleted mid-turn) — exactly one {type:'error', code:'chat_forbidden'} frame, no event data, onSubscriptionRevoked fires, the conversation leaves chatSubscriptions, and the Redis refcount is released.
A citation with resolvedNodeId: null whose nodeId is authorized — delivered unchanged, resolvedNodeId still null. A null resolvedNodeId is never itself a reason to drop a citation.
A citation whose nodeId is not in authorizedNodeIds — the whole citation is dropped; metrics.contextNodes and the other three counts are not recomputed.

A citation whose nodeId is authorized but whose non-null resolvedNodeId is not — the whole citation is dropped (the strict reading recorded in Ticket Check item 1), not half-delivered with a nulled pointer.
Every citation stripped — the chat.turn.completed frame is still delivered, with citations: [], the full answer, and unchanged metrics.
A chat subscribe frame before authentication — the existing generic {code:'unauthenticated'} frame, no subscription recorded, no Core call, no Redis SUBSCRIBE.
A chat subscribe frame on a gateway constructed without the chat deps — the generic chat_forbidden refusal (fail closed), never a silently-accepted unverified subscription.

Two connections owned by the same user subscribe to the same conversation (two browser tabs) — exactly one real Redis SUBSCRIBE; both receive every push; each gets its own authorization call per push; when one disconnects the channel stays subscribed; when the second disconnects a single UNSUBSCRIBE is issued.

Two subscribe frames for the same conversation arriving before the first authorization resolves — acquireChatChannel still fires exactly once and the refcount stays balanced against the single close-time release.
sendSafe on a socket whose readyState is CLOSED, or whose send throws — swallowed and logged, relayChatEvent still resolves.

Redis subscriber reconnect: ioredis re-issues SUBSCRIBE for its tracked channels on its own, so the gateway adds no reconnect logic; events published during the gap are not replayed (chat pub/sub is at-most-once) and CH-03's REST read is the documented catch-up path. Covered by an explicit comment plus a test asserting the bus does not attempt its own replay/buffer.

An event arrives for a conversation with no matching connection (nobody subscribed on this gateway instance, or only a wrong-org connection exists) — short-circuits with zero Core authorization calls and zero frames.

A malformed chat frame from the client — {type:'subscribe', channel:'chat'} with no conversationId, a blank/non-string conversationId, or channel:'graph' — the existing generic {code:'bad_frame'} reply, connection stays open, nothing recorded.

Progress events with a gap or a repeat in seq (e.g. 1, 3, 3) are relayed verbatim in arrival order — the gateway never reorders, renumbers, de-duplicates or buffers; seq interpretation belongs to CH-06.

nodeIds is [] (every progress and error push, and every subscribe-time check) — Core is still called for the ownership half of the re-filter, authorizedNodeIds is ignored, and Core skips the graph query entirely.
